predecessors.text: Eastern Cutch: the part of Kutch east of about 70.2 E

successors.name: Republic of India
successors.text: Cutch State of 19,725 km2 (1901): the Kutch mainland without the Rann

ledger.x: About 1147: Lakho Jadani founds the Kingdom of Kutch.
ledger.cp: Chawda and Chaulukya dynasties (the page's predecessors)

ledger.x: 1549: the capital moves from Lakhiarviro to Bhuj.

ledger.cp: Jadeja chieftains of Cutch (Jam Raval and others)

ledger.x: 25 December 1815: Anjar comes under British occupation.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)
British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 1 June 1948: Cutch is placed under the Government of India.

wars.name: Mughal invasion of Kutch
wars.outcome: In 1719 under Deshalji I the Mughal Viceroy of Gujarat invaded Kutch and his army was defeated after Naga Bawas joined the Kutch army.

wars.name: Kalhora attacks on Kutch
wars.outcome: Mian Ghulam Shah Kalhoro of Sindh "attacked Cutch twice once in 1763-64" and "again in 1765"; the page gives no result, and in 1770 a daughter of Wesuji was married to the Mian Kalhoro.

wars.name: Anglo-Gaekwad campaign against Kutch
wars.outcome: On 15 December 1815 the army of Cutch was defeated near Bhadreswar by combined British and Gaekwad forces; Anjar was occupied by the British from 25 December 1815 to 25 December 1822, when it reverted to Cutch by agreement; the Jadeja rulers accepted British…

certainty.note: The page gives no boundary; Eastern Cutch is a reading of "ruled Eastern Cutch".
The page gives 19,725 km2 (1901) and no boundary; the shape is the Kutch mainland polygon.
